viz.cloudMethods:
Cloud Sources and Styles

The clouds row has two independent axes: where cloud zones come from (Source), and how they are drawn (Style).

Sources

  • NWP — derived from the numerical weather prediction model's cloud cover parameterisation (low / mid / high bands). Shows where the model itself predicts clouds.
  • DD — derived from dewpoint depression in the sounding profile. When the gap between temperature and dewpoint is small (DD < 2°C), air is near saturation and cloud is likely. Sounding-based, independent of the model's cloud scheme.

Both sources can be enabled simultaneously for comparison. They often agree in moist layers but may differ where NWP sub-grid clouds or local moisture are present.

Styles

  • Soft — feathered gradient fills with coverage-proportional opacity (GRAMET-like).
  • Layer — classic hatched look. Hatch line spacing/width also varies by coverage class.
  • Square — solid filled cells per zone with no hatching, opacity from the same DD/cover% scale as Layer.
viz.convectionMethods:
Convective Methods

The cross-section offers two convective risk overlays:

  • Thermo — risk from thermodynamic indices (CAPE, CIN). Tower bounds from LFC/LCL (base) and EL (top). Zero risk when CAPE is zero, even if the NWP model parameterises convective clouds.
  • NWP — risk from the NWP model's native convective cloud parameterisation (GFS convective cover %). Tower bounds are model-computed convective base/top. This typically matches what GRAMET shows.

Enable both to compare. The advisory system uses whichever method you select in your profile settings.
viz.icingMethods:
Icing Methods

The cross-section offers three icing overlays, each combining an icing formula with a cloud detection method:

Formulas

  • Ogimet — continuous parabolic index peaking at −7°C. Maps temperature to an icing severity index across the 0 to −14°C range (layered) or 0 to −20°C (convective). Simple, well-proven in European GA.
  • SFIP — fuzzy-logic algorithm combining temperature, relative humidity, cloud liquid water, and vertical velocity via membership functions. More complex, uses direct NWP moisture data when available.

Cloud Signals

  • DD (dewpoint depression) — sounding-based. Uses a continuous cosine taper: full icing index at DD = 0, zero at DD ≥ 2°C. No NWP cloud data needed.
  • NWP (model cloud cover) — uses the NWP model's cloud cover percentage at each altitude. 50% cloud → 50% of icing index. This is the approach used by Autorouter GRAMET.

The Three Methods

  • Ogimet-DD — Ogimet formula + DD cloud signal
  • Ogimet-NWP — Ogimet formula + NWP cloud signal
  • SFIP-NWP — SFIP fuzzy-logic (inherently uses NWP moisture inputs)

Enable multiple methods to compare them side-by-side. The advisory system uses whichever method you select in your profile settings.

viz.obscurationMethod:
Surface obscuration

Cross-section pressure-level cloud detectors paint nothing for fog that lives below 1000 hPa (≈ a few hundred feet AGL at most inland fields). This layer synthesises a near-surface band whenever the surface forecast indicates reduced visibility or near-saturated low cloud — bridging the gap between the LIFR signal on the map and an empty pressure-level cross-section.

Triggers

  • Primary — surface visibility < 5 km. Severity tiers: LIFR purple (FG, <1 km), IFR red (BR/MIFG, 1–3 km), MVFR amber (BR, 3–5 km).
  • Secondary — for models without a visibility forecast (ECMWF / Météo-France / GEM): low cloud cover ≥ 80% AND surface dewpoint depression < 2°C. Severity grades by surface DD: < 0.5°C → LIFR (saturated, fog), else IFR.

Diagonal hatching is used (rather than horizontal cloud-style) to flag this as a visibility obstruction, not a cloud band.

settings.cruiseSpeedInfoBody:
Enter your cruise speed as indicated airspeed (IAS) in knots — the number you read off the ASI at cruise power.

For time and distance estimates we convert IAS to true airspeed (TAS), which is higher at altitude (roughly +2% per 1,000 ft). We use the ISA standard atmosphere at your selected cruise altitude, so changing the altitude updates the estimate.

help.startTourHint: A 9-step walkthrough on a real briefing — advisories, cross-section, route graph, Skew-T. Two minutes.
tour.welcome.title: Welcome to your briefing
tour.welcome.desc: This quick tour walks through the main parts of a flight briefing. You can hit Skip anytime — nothing here changes your flight.
tour.displayMode.title: Compact vs. full details
tour.displayMode.desc: The briefing opens compact by default. Switch to Details to unfold extra metrics, controls, and sections you can dig into.
tour.assessment.title: Overall assessment
tour.assessment.desc: The headline read on your flight: a colour-coded summary from the AI digest, combining advisories, observations, and forecast confidence.
tour.advisories.title: Route advisories
tour.advisories.desc: Deterministic hazard evaluators — icing, turbulence, convective, cloud, and model-agreement. Click any advisory for the underlying numbers and the rule that triggered it.
tour.crossSection.title: Cross-section
tour.crossSection.desc: A vertical slice along your route. Clouds, icing, turbulence, convective columns, and terrain — all on the same time/altitude grid.
tour.layers.title: Toggle layers
tour.layers.desc: Try it: click a checkbox to turn a layer on or off. The tour stays open — interact freely, then hit Next when you're ready.
tour.modelTheme.title: Compare models, themes & Windy
tour.modelTheme.desc: Switch model to see each weather model's cross-section, pick a theme to match your visual preference, and Open in Windy jumps to the highlighted location at that exact time for the selected model.
tour.layerInfo.title: Info on any metric
tour.layerInfo.desc: Every layer and metric has a ⓘ button. Click it for the formula, units, source model, and a colour-scale legend.
tour.routeGraph.title: Route graph metrics
tour.routeGraph.desc: Below the cross-section is a scalar graph along the route — wind, CAPE, ceiling, and more. Use these selectors to pick what to plot on the left and right axes.
tour.skewt.title: Skew-T at any point
tour.skewt.desc: Click any point on the cross-section to inspect its full sounding here — temperature, dewpoint, parcel path, CAPE/CIN, and overlay bands showing where clouds and icing live.
tour.done.title: That's the tour
tour.done.desc: Synopsis, GRAMET, Sounding Analysis, and Model Comparison are below if you want more depth. Have a safe flight.
tour.offer.text: New: take a quick guided tour of the briefing — it'll show you advisories, the cross-section, route graph, and Skew-T. About two minutes.
